newsitem.title: USA: Trial of former Ill. tollway agency head begins.
newsitem.headline: Trial of former Ill. tollway agency head begins.

text.p: The former head of Illinois State Toll Highway Authority and a state representative went on trial Tuesday on theft and conspiracy charges stemming from a tollway land sale, the Chicago Sun-Times reported Wednesday.

Robert Hickman, former executive director of the bond-issuing agency, and State Rep. Joseph Kotlarz, D-Chicago, are being tried in DuPage County Circuit Court. The charges involve a $240,000 commission on a 1992 land sale to Waste Management Inc., the Sun-Times reported.

Prosecutors allege that Hickman and Kotlarz told tollway officials that company had offered $3.8 million for the 12-acre parcel, then made up a phony $240,000 brokerage fee to hide the real $4.04 million sale price, the newspaper said.
Kotlarz allegedly received a portion of the brokerage fee from a real estate company, the paper reported.
Attorneys for Kotlarz and Hickman have denied the charges.
